conventions.convention: The metric signature is (-,+,+,+), the normal n is future unit timelike, and K(X,Y)=g(∇_X n,Y).
In a positively oriented future orthonormal frame, F(n,e_i)=-e_i and F(e_i,e_j)=ε_ijk b_k; the observer components e=E/c and b=B have units tesla.
The momentum constraint is D^j K_ji-D_i tr_h K=-(κ/μ0)(e×_h b)_i; the Hamiltonian constraint has electromagnetic source (κ/μ0)(|e|²+|b|²).

Circle coordinates transform by z_j=g_ij^{-1}z_i, normalized local forms satisfy a_j=a_i-i g_ij^{-1}dg_ij, and physical curvature is F=κ0 da_i with κ0>0 in webers. Connections are compared through their metric and field strength, without asserting uniqueness of connection representatives.
A Cauchy hypersurface meets each inextendible causal curve at exactly one parameter value.

Maximality means that every other development of the same complete data embeds into the maximal development; it concerns smooth globally hyperbolic developments and does not imply geodesic completeness.

The periodic Sobolev variable is the dimensionless torus coordinate θ; length coordinates are X=L0θ. Metric components lie in H^{s+1}, while K and electromagnetic component arrays lie in H^s, with integer s≥5 and a uniform positive metric lower bound.

The selected matter configuration space is a singleton and its action is identically zero, so current and matter stress vanish. The conclusions are conditional model deductions with no empirical premises.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let (M,g,N) be a smooth time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, and let i:Σ→M be a smooth spacelike Cauchy embedding. If F and F̄ are smooth closed two-forms with i*F=i*F̄, then there is a globally defined smooth one-form α with dα=F−F̄.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, smooth constrained electrovacuum data on a nonempty smooth oriented boundaryless three-manifold, with the stated positive constants, SI conventions, and supplied compatible normalized initial circle-connection data, admit a smooth local development in the zero-matter action branch on a possibly variable-width globally hyperbolic Cauchy neighborhood. Its physical curvature lies in the supplied bundle sector and induces exactly e,b. Developments are related near the initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry carrying g and F. For smooth periodic data satisfying the stated H^{s+1}/H^s conditions, s≥5, and positive metric lower bound, the solution has the displayed L∞ and C0 Sobolev regularities on its common local interval. No uniform noncompact time width, global-time existence, maximal-development conclusion, or physical validity is asserted.

For a smooth spacelike embedding i:Σ→M in a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with a supplied smooth future unit normal n, each p∈Σ has neighborhoods U_p,V_p and ε_p>0 such that Φ_p(t,x)=γ_{i(x),n_{i(x)}}(t) is a diffeomorphism from (−ε_p,ε_p)×U_p onto V_p. Its differential at (0,p) is (a,X)↦a n_{i(p)}+di_p(X). No global injectivity or uniform width is asserted.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, nonempty connected smooth oriented boundaryless constrained electrovacuum data with the stated constants and compatible initial normalized circle-connection data admit a smooth connected globally hyperbolic maximal field-strength development in the zero-matter action branch. Its F is physical curvature in the transported initial bundle sector. Every other smooth globally hyperbolic stationary development of the same complete data embeds into it preserving time orientation, the initial embedding, g and F. Any two maximal developments are related by exactly one data-fixing isometry of (g,F). The maximality is restricted to the smooth globally hyperbolic class.

alerts.finding: Definition (e) gives H⁺(S)=D⁺(S)∖I⁻(D⁺(S)), then describes it as points 'not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)'. The prose reverses the relation: def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability (c) defines I⁻(A)={p: there exists q∈A with p≪q}. The displayed subtraction therefore excludes points that chronologically precede a point of D⁺(S), rather than points preceded by one. The assigned proofs use the Cauchy-intersection clause, not this horizon prose.
